request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: N/A
Age: 24
Gender: Female
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted to our hospital with acute pulmonary edema due to severe aortic valve insufficiency. She had previously been diagnosed with Takayasu's disease and had undergone multiple surgeries, including replacement of the distal ascending aorta and hemiarch, stenosis of celiac artery and superior mesenteric artery, and stenosis of the orifices of both renal arteries. She had a graft used to direct blood flow from the right internal iliac artery to all stenosed arteries. She also underwent a right nephrectomy due to acute thrombosis of the right renal artery graft. The patient was on steroid treatment since the diagnosis of her disease.

Treatment:
The patient underwent surgery to address the aortic valve insufficiency. The procedure was performed through a median sternotomy, and a composite graft with a mechanical valve was implanted. The patient's postoperative course was uneventful, and she was discharged from the hospital on the 10th postoperative day.

Follow-up:
The patient had a one year clinical follow-up that showed normal echocardiographical results, and she was doing well in normal daily activities.

Pathology:
Part of the dilated aortic root wall was sent for histological examination, which verified the diagnosis of Takayasu's arteritis.

Note:
The patient's condition was complex and required surgery to address the aortic valve insufficiency. The patient's postoperative course was uneventful, and she had a good one year clinical follow-up.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
The episode was an admission for acute pulmonary edema caused by severe aortic valve insufficiency, treated with a composite graft and mechanical valve. The underlying cause is Takayasu's arteritis, which is coded M31.4 (aortic arch syndrome). The question is whether the principal diagnosis is the aortic regurgitation or the arteritis.

ICD-10 has a dagger-asterisk convention for aortic valve disorders in systemic disease, but Takayasu's arteritis is not one of those combinations. Aortic valve insufficiency in this case is a manifestation of the aortitis, so the choices are:

- I35.1 (nonrheumatic aortic insufficiency)
- I71 (aortic aneurysm/dilation)
- M31.4 (Takayasu's)

The condition that occasioned the admission and was treated by surgery was the severe aortic regurgitation. The treatment was directed at the valve, and the hospital resources went to the valve and root replacement. The arteritis was a chronic, known background condition, so under the Australian principal diagnosis rule the valve disease is the better choice. Pulmonary edema is a symptom of the valve failure and does not take priority.

I35 is the category: nonrheumatic aortic valve disorders, with I35.1 for insufficiency.

CODE: I35
